rows.citation: Druckmann S, Berger TK, Schürmann F, et al. (2011). Effective Stimuli for Constructing Reliable Neuron Models. PLoS Computational Biology 7(8): e1002133.
rows.model_type: Multicompartment conductance-based cortical neuron models (NEURON), with conductance densities fitted to experimental recordings
rows.controlled_mutations: no - compares stimuli by how well they constrain fitted conductance densities; no injected faults or edited model variants.
rows.multiple_stimuli: yes - depolarizing steps, ramps and two noisy current types at several intensities, injected repeatedly into real cells and models.
rows.electrophysiology_features: yes - feature-based errors (e.g. firing rate, AP height) scored against experimental mean and SD; spike-timing coincidence factor for noisy inputs.
rows.protocol_optimization: partial - systematically compares training stimulus sets by generalisation error; no budgeted search algorithm; an optimal minimal set is named as a future goal.
rows.heldout_evaluation: partial - fitted models are tested on stimuli withheld from fitting; no held-out models or held-out fault families.
rows.ai_transformations: no - no AI-generated or AI-edited models or code.
rows.software: none (custom NSGA-II optimisation implemented in NEURON; no released package identified)
rows.distinction_from_neurosem: Druckmann ranks stimuli for constraining fits to data. NeuroSem would select a compact battery for detecting seeded single-fault edits, with refinement-calibrated tolerances, testing it on held-out models and a held-out mutation family.
rows.verification_method: Crossref works API (metadata, 6 authors incl. Segev I); Europe PMC REST search (abstract, PMID 21876663, PMC3158041); Europe PMC fullTextXML (methods: stimuli, NSGA-II, training vs generalisation sets, Table 1).
rows.found_via: WebSearch 'active selection of stimuli to distinguish neuron models'; Europe PMC refined query; DOI via NCBI idconv; abstract via Europe PMC

rows.citation: Apgar JF, Toettcher JE, Endy D, et al. (2008). Stimulus Design for Model Selection and Validation in Cell Signaling. PLoS Computational Biology 4(2): e30.
rows.model_type: Mass-action kinetic ODE models of cell signalling (antibody-ligand binding, MAPK, EGFR pathway)
rows.controlled_mutations: partial - builds closely related alternative models (added or changed mechanisms, refit to the same step response); not systematic single-fault mutation families.
rows.multiple_stimuli: partial - a model-based controller designs a time-varying input for each candidate model; contrasted with step responses, not a battery of standard protocols.
rows.electrophysiology_features: no - outputs are species concentration trajectories in signalling networks; no neurons or electrophysiology features.
rows.protocol_optimization: yes - stimuli come from controller optimisation (MATLAB fmincon) that drives outputs to a target trajectory, discriminating the candidate models.
rows.heldout_evaluation: no - evaluated in simulation on constructed candidate-model sets; no held-out model or fault-family split reported.
rows.ai_transformations: no - no AI-generated or AI-edited models.
rows.software: none (MATLAB implementation described in methods; no released package identified)
rows.distinction_from_neurosem: Apgar designs a bespoke input for each candidate signalling model to tell models apart. NeuroSem would pick one compact, rheobase-normalised electrophysiology battery from mutant detection data and test whether it transfers to unseen neuron models and fault families.
rows.verification_method: Crossref works API (metadata, 5 authors, vol 4 issue 2 e30); Europe PMC REST search (abstract, PMID 18282085, PMC2323406); Europe PMC fullTextXML (methods: candidate/perturbed models, fmincon).
rows.found_via: WebSearch 'automatic stimulation protocol selection model validation'; Europe PMC refined 'stimulus design' query; Crossref

rows.citation: Jæger KH, Wall S, Tveito A (2019). Detecting undetectables: Can conductances of action potential models be changed without appreciable change in the transmembrane potential? Chaos: An Interdisciplinary Journal of Nonlinear Science 29(7): 073102.
rows.model_type: Cardiac action potential ionic-current ODE models
rows.controlled_mutations: partial - studies changes to maximal conductances via SVD of an ionic-current matrix; parameter perturbations, not recorded edit or mutation operators.
rows.multiple_stimuli: partial - abstract says stimulation protocol choice can improve identifiability; protocol details not checked (full text not retrieved).
rows.electrophysiology_features: unclear - abstract refers to action potential and ionic currents; whether scalar electrophysiology features are used was not verified.
rows.protocol_optimization: partial - abstract reports using the stimulation protocol to improve identifiability; extent of any systematic optimisation unverified.
rows.heldout_evaluation: unclear - abstract describes no held-out models or perturbation families; full text not retrieved.
rows.ai_transformations: no - no AI-generated or AI-edited models.
rows.distinction_from_neurosem: Asks whether conductance changes can be nearly invisible in cardiac voltage, framed as parameter identifiability. NeuroSem would test edited neuron model files, using multiple protocols, calibrated feature tolerances and a battery evaluated on held-out models.
rows.verification_method: Crossref works API (metadata and abstract); Europe PMC REST search (abstract, PMID 31370420); OpenAlex works API (OA locations). Full text not retrieved (DUO repository page returned no PDF link).
rows.found_via: Europe PMC refined query 'identifiability AND protocol/stimulus AND ion channel/action potential'; abstract via Europe PMC

rows.citation: Marin B, Gleeson P (2026). OSB Model Validation (OMV), version 0.4.0 [software]. GitHub repository OpenSourceBrain/osb-model-validation; PyPI package OSBModelValidation.
rows.model_type: NeuroML2/LEMS and other Open Source Brain models run on multiple simulator engines (e.g. jNeuroML, jNeuroML_NEURON)
rows.controlled_mutations: no - checks models against user-written expected values; no mutant generation or fault injection.
rows.multiple_stimuli: partial - a MEP file can list several user-authored experiments; no standard or generated protocol battery.
rows.electrophysiology_features: partial - analyzers cover spike times, resting potential, input resistance, rates and time series, compared elementwise rather than as an eFEL feature set.
rows.protocol_optimization: no - no selection or optimisation of experiments or stimuli.
rows.heldout_evaluation: no - continuous-integration regression checks; no held-out evaluation design.
rows.ai_transformations: no - no AI-generated or AI-edited models.
rows.software: OSB Model Validation, https://github.com/OpenSourceBrain/osb-model-validation (PyPI OSBModelValidation 0.4.0, LGPL-3.0-only per PyPI; GitHub API reports LGPL-3.0)
rows.distinction_from_neurosem: OMV is the saved-output regression baseline NeuroSem would reuse. Tolerances are hand-set per observable (numpy allclose relative tolerance, default 0.1). NeuroSem would add refinement-calibrated feature tolerances, seeded mutants and selected multi-protocol batteries.
rows.verification_method: GitHub REST API (repo metadata, license, file tree); raw GitHub README.md and source (omv/analyzers/analyzer.py, spikes.py, utils/timeseries.py, schemata/types/protocol.yaml); PyPI JSON API (version, license, authors, release dates).
rows.found_via: WebSearch 'OSB Model Validation OMV osb-model-validation GitHub repository'; PyPI JSON

rows.citation: Brillout A, He N, Mazzucchi M, et al. (2010). Mutation-Based Test Case Generation for Simulink Models. In: Formal Methods for Components and Objects, Lecture Notes in Computer Science, pp. 208-227. Springer Berlin Heidelberg.
rows.model_type: Simulink control-software models translated to ANSI-C (discrete-step, floating-point), analysed by bounded model checking
rows.controlled_mutations: yes - single syntactic mutations and injected faults (e.g. signal stuck-at-0), each toggled by a flag in one combined model.
rows.multiple_stimuli: partial - generates input vectors (test cases) that expose each mutant; generic signal inputs, not physiological stimulation protocols.
rows.electrophysiology_features: no - compares raw output signals of the original and mutant models.
rows.protocol_optimization: yes - aims for small test suites by maximising the number of mutations each test case covers.
rows.heldout_evaluation: no - paper states experimental evaluation of its techniques is planned future work.
rows.ai_transformations: no - no AI-generated or AI-edited models.
rows.software: Cover, a test-generation tool built on the CBMC model checker (named in the paper; no public URL verified)
rows.distinction_from_neurosem: This is formal, SAT-based mutant-killing test generation for discrete Simulink programs, with equivalence checking. NeuroSem would be empirical and simulation-based: continuous neuron dynamics, eFEL features with calibrated tolerances, and a greedy battery tested on held-out models and a held-out mutation family.
rows.verification_method: Crossref works API (metadata: 7 authors incl. Weissenbacher G, which the input list omitted; LNCS pp. 208-227, issued 2010); Semantic Scholar Graph API (DBLP key conf/fmco/BrilloutHMKPRW09, OA link); OpenAlex works API; author-hosted PDF (philipp.ruemmer.org) read for methods.
rows.found_via: WebSearch 'model-based mutation testing Simulink test generation to kill mutants'; WebSearch site:semanticscholar.org fallback; Crossref title query

rows.citation: Omote M (2026). Silent numerical failures in large language model-generated pharmacokinetic simulation code: a benchmark against target-controlled infusion validation criteria using the Marsh propofol model. medRxiv (preprint, not peer reviewed).
rows.model_type: Three-compartment pharmacokinetic ODE (Marsh propofol model), with Python simulation code written by LLMs
rows.controlled_mutations: no - errors arise naturally in LLM-written code; no seeded fault operators.
rows.multiple_stimuli: no - single standardized 120-minute bolus-plus-infusion dosing regimen.
rows.electrophysiology_features: no - plasma concentration accuracy metrics (MDPE, MDAPE, Wobble); not neurons.
rows.protocol_optimization: no - no selection of dosing regimens or tests.
rows.heldout_evaluation: no - benchmarks 200 runs from five LLMs over two prompt phases against one reference; no held-out split.
rows.ai_transformations: yes - LLM-generated simulation code; reports runs that execute but diverge silently (unit/time-scale, duplicated-bolus bugs).
rows.distinction_from_neurosem: Relevant only to RQ7, the AI lens. NeuroSem's optional agent case study would test isolated edits to neuron models with a hidden multi-protocol battery, not code written from scratch and checked under one regimen.
rows.verification_method: Crossref works API (posted-content, institution medRxiv, CC BY 4.0, abstract); bioRxiv/medRxiv details API (title, author, affiliation, 2026-04-28, v1, health informatics); Europe PMC REST search (record present).
rows.found_via: Crossref 'silent semantic errors code generated by large language models'; Europe PMC; verified via Crossref + Europe PMC abstract
